nameStory: The white-fronted amazon gets its name from the bright white patch of feathers that covers its forehead and extends around its eyes like a mask. This distinctive white 'front' makes it look like it's wearing spectacles, which is why it's also called the spectacled amazon parrot.
description: The white-fronted amazon is a medium-sized tropical parrot from Central America that occasionally shows up in New England as an escaped pet. These colorful birds are primarily green with a distinctive white forehead patch and blue-tinged flight feathers. They're intelligent birds known for their ability to mimic dozens of different sounds, and like most large parrots, they can live for around 40 years.

idTips.label: White forehead patch
idTips.description: Bright white feathers covering the forehead and wrapping around the eyes like spectacles - this is the bird's signature feature

idTips.label: Green body plumage
idTips.description: Predominantly bright green feathers covering most of the body, giving it the classic parrot appearance

idTips.label: Blue wing patches
idTips.description: Blue-tinged flight feathers visible when wings are spread or during flight

idTips.label: Vocal mimicry
idTips.description: Can produce a wide variety of sounds, calls, and even human speech - much more diverse than native New England birds

idTips.label: Chunky parrot build
idTips.description: Stocky body with a large curved beak typical of parrots, very different from any native New England bird

habitat: White-fronted amazons are not native to New England and don't establish wild populations here due to the cold climate. Any sighting would be an escaped or released pet bird, most likely spotted in suburban areas near homes, parks, or bird feeders where it might seek food and shelter.

seasonality.spring: Escaped birds might be more visible as they search for food and mates, potentially calling loudly from trees or power lines.
seasonality.summer: Most likely season to spot an escapee, as the warm weather allows these tropical birds to survive temporarily outdoors.
seasonality.fall: Any sightings become increasingly rare as cooler temperatures make survival difficult for these tropical birds.
seasonality.winter: Extremely unlikely to survive New England winters outdoors - any winter sighting would indicate a very recently escaped bird in immediate need of rescue.

funFact: White-fronted amazons can learn to imitate 30 to 40 different sounds - not just human words, but also household noises like microwaves beeping, dogs barking, and even the specific ringtone of their owner's phone!
confusionNotes: In New England, there's really no native bird that looks like a white-fronted amazon - the bright green coloring and white forehead are unlike anything in our local bird community. If you see what looks like a tropical parrot, it's definitely an escaped pet.
contextualKnowledge: White-fronted amazons are popular pets but require experienced care and can live for decades. Any sighting in New England represents an escaped bird that likely cannot survive our climate long-term and should be reported to local wildlife authorities or bird rescue organizations.
compareHints: Since no other amazon parrots are found in New England, compare this to other escaped pet parrots that might occasionally be seen. White-fronted amazons are distinguished from other parrots by their specific combination of green body, white forehead patch, and medium size - they're larger than cockatiels or parakeets but smaller than macaws.
